headline: Apple runs a giant model across several Mac Studios
dek: The new MLX version splits a model of nearly 816 billion parameters across Macs, Apple Machine Learning says.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A giant model off the cloud
body: Apple released a new MLX version with distributed inference across several Mac Studios (Apple Machine Learning).
According to the company, four units run Muse Spark Open, nearly 816 billion parameters, at over 36 tokens per second (Apple Machine Learning).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: What makes it possible
s3.body: According to Apple Machine Learning, it relies on:

points.t: RDMA over Thunderbolt 5, from macOS 26.2 (Apple Machine Learning).
New MLX communication collectives split the work (Apple Machine Learning).
Each Mac runs part of the model's layers, Apple says.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: What the M5 chip changes
body: According to Apple, the M5 Ultra produces the first token up to 4.6 times faster than the M3 Ultra.
Text generation is 1.6 times higher on the M5 Ultra, with 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth, per Apple Machine Learning.

stat.cap: parameters in the largest model, Apple says

items.t: The company published the MLX LM used in testing.
mlx.launch starts the program on many machines, Apple says.
MLX is free; the cost is the hardware, the company says.

caption.hook: Apple shows a model of nearly 816 billion parameters running across several Mac Studios.
body: According to Apple Machine Learning, the new MLX version enables distributed inference: four Mac Studios run Muse Spark Open at over 36 tokens per second. It builds on an RDMA driver over Thunderbolt 5 and new jaccl communication collectives.

The company says the M5 Ultra produces the first token up to 4.6 times faster than the M3 Ultra. MLX is free and open source, and the cost sits in the hardware. All figures come from Apple's own tests.
caption.cta: Would you run a giant AI model on a stack of Macs at home?
